epics.title: Verifiable Authentication Boundary
epics.jtbd: When an epidemiologist authenticates, I want the system to verify my credentials against a persistent source of truth, so that unauthorized access to the epidemiological data is prevented.
requirements: R1: A backend authentication endpoint must verify credentials and issue secure JWT tokens.
R2: The frontend login flow must invoke the backend authentication endpoint rather than directly setting client-side state.
R3: Protected backend API routes must strictly require and validate the JWT before granting access.
R4: End-to-end tests must confirm successful authentication grants access and invalid credentials reject access.

slices.title: Authentication API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the authentication API contract for this epic, I want a shared OpenAPI definition for credential submission and token issuance, so that backend and frontend parallel work is synchronized.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a need for authentication
When the frontend and backend interact
Then they must adhere to the defined OpenAPI schema for the login endpoint
Given a token response
When defining the contract
Then the JWT structure must be explicitly specified

slices.title: Authentication Domain Data Model
slices.jtbd: When implementing the authentication data model for this epic, I want structured storage for user credentials and roles, so that identity claims can be verified against a source of truth.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a login attempt
When the backend verifies the user
Then the user credentials must be queried from a structured persistence layer
Given user roles
When defining the schema
Then the roles must be properly normalized

slices.title: Backend JWT Verification Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing backend authentication for this epic, I want token generation and validation middleware, so that sensitive data routes are protected from unauthorized access.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given valid credentials
When a user logs in
Then the server must issue a cryptographically signed JWT
Given an unauthorized request
When the user accesses a protected route without a valid token
Then the server must return a 401 Unauthorized

slices.title: Frontend Secure Authentication Flow
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend authentication for this epic, I want the login form to utilize the new backend endpoint, so that identity is verified rather than assumed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the user enters credentials
When they submit the login form
Then the frontend must send a request to the backend authentication API
Given a successful login
When the token is received
Then it must be securely stored and attached to subsequent API requests

slices.title: Authentication Boundary Validation
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA coverage for this epic, I want automated verification of the authentication flow, so that the boundary integrity is continuously proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a running application
When E2E tests exercise the login form with valid credentials
Then the system must grant access to the protected data
Given invalid credentials
When the tests attempt to log in
Then access must be explicitly denied and an error shown

epics.title: Disable Unsupported Mock Capabilities
epics.jtbd: When a researcher uses the application, I want unsupported UI features to be hidden or disabled, so that I am not misled by non-functional simulated actions.
requirements: R1: Identify and disable or remove the file upload UI components that lack backend implementation.
R2: Identify and disable or remove the dossier generation UI components that lack backend implementation.
R3: Ensure the UI correctly reflects only genuinely functional capabilities to the user without confusing mock timeouts.
R4: Test coverage must verify that disabled features cannot be accessed or triggered by the user.

slices.title: Frontend Mock Capability Removal
slices.jtbd: When implementing capability removal for this epic, I want to disable the upload modal and dossier generation features, so that users do not experience false functionality.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the application UI
When viewing the interface
Then the file upload modal must not be accessible
Given the dossier generation feature
When an action is taken
Then it must be fully disabled or hidden

slices.title: QA Verification for Disabled Features
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA coverage for this epic, I want automated verification that mock capabilities are disabled, so that users are never exposed to incomplete features.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the application UI
When E2E tests attempt to locate the file upload and dossier generation elements
Then they must not be present or must be strictly disabled
Given automated testing
When executed
Then the absence of mock simulated behaviors must be verified
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Test pass rate for hidden elements

epics.title: Persistent Domain Ontology Architecture
epics.jtbd: When an epidemiologist queries the archive, I want the system to operate on a rigorously structured, physically persisted domain model, so that data integrity and conceptual boundaries are mathematically preserved.
requirements: R1: Define normalized SQL reference tables for organizations, document types, and hazard categories.
R2: Implement a unified database persistence layer replacing purely hardcoded memory stubs.
R3: Create a Dossier aggregate root managing the lifecycle of its component documents.
R4: Establish a core architectural framework with bounded contexts for Catalog, Telemetry, and Privacy.
R5: E2E and integration tests must confirm domain entities are correctly persisted and boundaries are maintained.

slices.title: Normalized Ontology Database Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the persistence schema for this epic, I want normalized SQL tables for the domain model, so that categorical data and entities have a physical reality.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the database schema
When migrations are run
Then normalized reference tables for organizations, document types, and hazard categories must be created
Given the Dossier aggregate
When configured
Then foreign key relationships must enforce part-whole structural integrity

slices.title: Bounded Context API Contracts
slices.jtbd: When implementing the API contracts for this epic, I want cleanly demarcated OpenAPI specifications for each bounded context, so that distinct operational domains do not bleed into one another.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API surface
When contracts are defined
Then Catalog, Telemetry, and Privacy must have separate, isolated specifications
Given the frontend and backend integration
When parallel development starts
Then both teams must build against these distinct contracts

slices.title: Persistent Domain Backend Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend domain architecture for this epic, I want a robust data access layer serving persisted entities, so that the application no longer relies on mock memory data.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given API requests for documents
When the backend processes them
Then it must query the physical database tables instead of static arrays
Given the core architectural framework
When configured
Then dependency injection and contextual boundaries must be strictly enforced

slices.title: Frontend Bounded Context State Management
slices.jtbd: When implementing frontend architecture for this epic, I want state separated by bounded context and fetching real persisted data, so that the monolithic global state is dismantled.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the frontend application
When state is initialized
Then it must be scoped separately for Catalog, Telemetry, and Privacy rather than mixed
Given data fetching
When requesting documents
Then the frontend must invoke the newly defined API endpoints rather than hardcoded client lists

slices.title: Domain Ontology QA Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA coverage for this epic, I want automated verification of the persistent model, so that architectural boundaries and data integrity are continuously proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the persistent domain model
When integration tests run
Then database queries must correctly read and write normalized data without mock reliance
Given bounded contexts
When tested end-to-end
Then boundaries must remain isolated and strictly enforced
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Test pass rate for persistence boundaries
